cases.name: S1: 'pasok' alone matches class, classes and classroom
cases.question: Pasok?
cases.why: and_v4: 'class' substring in rows 13 (classroom, by design), 3 (classes only), 4, 6, 7, 9; one word each, newest first. and_v3: no row has 'pasok'

cases.name: S2: 'pasok' with another word (AND)
cases.question: May pasok ba sa November 30?
cases.why: class AND november: rows 3 (2026) and 9 (2025); words [pasok] + date 11-30 = 4 each; tie, newest first

cases.name: S3: v1 synonyms kept ('klase')
cases.question: May klase ba?
cases.why: 'klase' -> 'class' is in v1 and v2; the same under both

cases.name: S4: rank_v1 finds the question word 'pasok' through the synonym under and_v4 only
cases.question: Kailan ang pasok ng make-up classes?
cases.why: words [pasok, make, up, classes]; row 6 has class+make+up+classes, row 7 class+make+up; and_v3 never finds 'pasok'

cases.name: S5: the taglish-08 shape: a date anchor does not pull in a non-matching row
cases.question: May pasok ba sa November 16-18?
cases.why: anchors 11-16 and 18 are in row 1 and row 11 only, which have no 'class'; every matching row scores 1

cases.name: S6: 'pasok' as a question word but not in the query
cases.question: Kailan ang pasok sa library?
cases.why: words [pasok, library]: rows 1 and 11 have 'library' but no 'class', so 1 point each under both matchers; the tie goes to the newer row 11 (2026-11-09T15:00) before row 1 (09:00)

cases.name: S7: the search's own ranking uses the v2 synonyms under and_v4
cases.question: Pasok ba sa november?
cases.why: words [pasok, november] (no day, so no date). and_v4: rows 3 and 9 find pasok via class and november = 2; rows 11 and 1 november only = 1; newest breaks ties. and_v3 (or rank with v1 synonyms): every row 1, newest first.
